answers.explanation: Each switch port is its own link with exactly two ends.
Every home in the neighborhood transmits on the same cable back to the provider.
Both frames are lost and have to be sent again.
The signaling about who may speak competes for the same medium as the data.
TDMA, FDMA, and CDMA give each node an exclusive piece.
ALOHA and the CSMA protocols are random access.
Each node has exclusive use of its own slot, band, or code, so they never collide.
A quiet node's share of the channel is wasted even when others have plenty to send.
A token passes from node to node, and only the holder may transmit.
